title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
authors_zh: Chang Ma、Junlei Zhang、Zhihao Zhu、Cheng Yang、Yujiu Yang、Yaohui Jin 等（The University of Hong Kong 等）
paper_type_zh: Agent 环境 / 工具使用数据与评测
best_for_zh: 研究 tool-use、agent trajectory、环境反馈契约和可复现评测的读者
one_line: AgentBoard contributes a tool-use or agent-environment surface with an explicit evaluation or verification contract.
AgentBoard 提供带明确评测契约的智能体环境评测面，除任务成功率外还用进度指标刻画多轮交互中的逐步推进。
why: It makes the action schema, environment state, and success predicate visible enough for reasoning-data curation and audit.
inclusion_reason: AgentBoard exposes an agent/tool environment or trajectory-like data object with a concrete feedback contract: Task success is supplemented by progress-rate metrics that capture incremental advancement during multi-turn interaction.

title: Problem
问题
html:
AgentBoard asks how to evaluate multi-turn LLM agents when final success alone hides partial progress and failure location. The primary source is "AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents" (arXiv:2401.13178, NeurIPS 2024 Oral), with the paper-linked official repository at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/AgentBoard. The evaluation surface is a partially observable interactive episode in one of nine environments, drawn from 1,012 curated tasks, where the agent observes state, acts, receives environment feedback, and is scored by success plus process-oriented metrics.

The decision boundary is agent evaluation and diagnostic benchmarking, not a training corpus and not a generic leaderboard detached from environment traces. AgentBoard is useful for the atlas because it makes progress within a trajectory part of the feedback contract: a model can fail the terminal task while still receiving measurable partial-progress evidence. Reuse requires pinning task versions, repository revision, model/scaffold settings, API behavior, parsing rules, and the exact definition of progress metrics.

AgentBoard 要解决的问题是：多轮 LLM agent 只看最终成功率会遮蔽中间进展和失败位置，应如何做可诊断评测。一手来源是《AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents》（arXiv:2401.13178，NeurIPS 2024 Oral）以及论文脚注给出的官方仓库 https://github.com/hkust-nlp/AgentBoard。评测对象是在 9 个环境、1,012 个 curated tasks 中的一条部分可观测交互 episode：agent 观察状态、采取动作、接收环境反馈，并由成功率和过程指标共同评分。

这张卡的边界是 agent 评测与诊断 benchmark，不是训练语料，也不是脱离轨迹的泛化排行榜。它对 atlas 的价值在于把“过程中是否推进任务”纳入反馈契约：模型可能最终失败，但仍能留下可度量的 partial-progress 证据。复用前要固定任务版本、仓库 revision、模型/scaffold、API 行为、解析规则和 progress metric 的精确定义。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
The one-sentence contribution is an analytical board for multi-turn agents that unifies diverse environments and adds fine-grained progress-rate metrics beyond final success. The core mechanism treats each benchmark as a partially observable interaction process, logs the trajectory, and measures both whether the task is solved and how much of the intended path the agent completed.

Closest comparisons are AgentBench-style success-rate suites and single-domain web/tool benchmarks. AgentBoard changes the audit object from "did the agent finish?" to "what progress did the agent make before termination?" The direction label is diagnostic agent evaluation. What is not new is running LLMs in interactive environments; the new reusable piece is the progress-aware scoring layer tied to trajectory analysis.

一句话贡献：AgentBoard 是一个面向多轮 agent 的分析型评测板，把多种环境统一起来，并在最终成功率之外加入细粒度 progress-rate 指标。核心机制是把每个 benchmark 视为部分可观测交互过程，记录轨迹，同时衡量任务是否完成以及模型在终止前推进了多少关键步骤。

最接近的对照是 AgentBench 式成功率套件和单领域 web/tool benchmark。AgentBoard 的变化是把审计对象从“是否完成”扩展为“终止前推进到了哪里”。方向标签是诊断型 agent 评测。它并不是首次让 LLM 跑交互环境；可复用的新层是和轨迹分析绑定的 progress-aware scoring。

title: Method
方法
html:
1. Inputs: a task from one of the nine environments, an initial observation, the available action interface, the chosen LLM agent scaffold, and metric definitions for final success and progress.
  2. Pipeline: run the agent in the environment; parse each response into an action; execute the action; record observation, action, and environment feedback; stop at task completion, failure, max turns, or timeout; compute final and process metrics.
  3. Outputs: trajectories, terminal success/failure, progress-rate or analogous process scores, and environment/model aggregate tables.
  4. Verifier and judge: environment implementations decide state transitions and terminal success; progress metrics encode task-specific partial completion rather than relying only on a free-form LLM judge.

For reproducibility, the exact repository commit, 1,012-task snapshot, environment dependencies, action parsers, prompts, model versions, max turns, tool/API credentials, and failure handling rules must be recorded. A progress score is only comparable if the same decomposition of task progress is used.

1. 输入：9 个环境之一的任务、初始 observation、可用动作接口、选定的 LLM agent scaffold，以及最终成功和过程进展指标定义。
  2. 流程：让 agent 在环境中运行；把每次回复解析成动作；执行动作；记录 observation、action 和环境反馈；在完成、失败、达到最大轮数或超时时停止；计算最终指标和过程指标。
  3. 输出：轨迹、终止成功/失败、progress-rate 或同类过程分数，以及按环境和模型聚合的表格。
  4. 验收者：环境实现决定状态转移和终止成功；progress metric 编码任务特定的部分完成度，而不是只依赖自由文本 LLM judge。

复现时必须记录仓库 commit、1,012 任务快照、环境依赖、动作解析器、prompt、模型版本、最大轮数、工具/API 凭据和失败处理规则。只有使用同一套任务进展分解时，progress score 才可比较。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
The paper reports experiments across nine environments and 1,012 tasks, comparing closed and open LLM agents under the same board. A key empirical claim is that progress-oriented metrics reveal behavior hidden by binary task success, including cases where an agent reaches useful intermediate states but misses the final condition. The authors also report that open-source models can exceed GPT-3.5 in parts of the evaluation while still trailing GPT-4 overall.

The row-level evidence is a trajectory with environment observations, actions, terminal outcome, and metric computation. This supports diagnostic analysis better than a single pass/fail label, but it remains bounded by the benchmark's task decomposition and metric implementation. Reported scores should not be reused without the same tasks, prompts, model snapshots, environment code, and turn/budget limits.

论文在 9 个环境、1,012 个任务上比较闭源和开源 LLM agent。关键实证结论是：过程型指标能揭示二元成功率看不到的行为，例如 agent 已到达有用中间状态但未满足最终条件。作者还报告部分开源模型在若干评测面上超过 GPT-3.5，但总体仍落后 GPT-4。

行级证据是一条包含 observation、action、终止结果和指标计算的轨迹。这比单一 pass/fail 更适合诊断，但仍受任务分解和 metric 实现约束。复用分数时必须保持同样的任务、prompt、模型快照、环境代码和轮数/预算限制。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
The prior-work baseline is success-rate evaluation in interactive agent benchmarks. AgentBoard changes the scoring contract by adding progress-aware metrics and framing tasks as partially observable decision processes. The direction signal is that agent benchmarks should expose failure location and partial achievement, not only terminal completion.

The quality signal is the combination of a paper-described framework, 1,012 curated tasks, and an official code/data repository. What is not new is the idea of testing LLMs in tool and web environments. Before reuse, inspect whether progress annotations are task-specific, whether task versions changed, how failures/timeouts are encoded, whether API-backed environments drift, and whether public tasks have contaminated later models.

已有工作基线主要是交互式 agent benchmark 中的成功率评测。AgentBoard 改变了评分契约：加入 progress-aware metrics，并把任务表述成部分可观测决策过程。方向信号是 agent benchmark 应暴露失败位置和部分完成度，而不只报告终止成功。

质量信号是论文中的框架、1,012 个 curated tasks，以及官方代码/数据仓库共同存在。不是新的部分是让 LLM 在工具和 web 环境中测试。复用前要检查 progress 标注是否任务特定、任务版本是否改变、失败/超时如何编码、API 环境是否漂移，以及公开任务是否污染后续模型。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
The progress metric is only as valid as the task decomposition behind it. If partial steps are hand-designed, incomplete, or too coarse, the metric may reward apparent progress that does not correspond to robust task solving. Terminal success and progress scores also depend on parsers, environment implementations, turn limits, and API/tool behavior.

AgentBoard should not be read as a universal measure of agent intelligence or as a stable result independent of release date. License terms, hidden or changed task sets, dependency versions, model snapshots, prompts, and public-data contamination remain separate audit targets.

progress metric 的有效性取决于背后的任务分解。如果部分步骤是人工设计、不完整或过粗，指标可能奖励表面进展，而不代表稳健完成任务。终止成功率和 progress score 也依赖解析器、环境实现、轮数限制和 API/工具行为。

不要把 AgentBoard 读成通用 agent 智能度量，也不要把结果读成脱离发布日期的稳定结论。license、隐藏或变更的任务集、依赖版本、模型快照、prompt 和公开数据污染仍是单独审计项。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
AgentBoard is useful as a schema for diagnostic trajectory evaluation. A reusable record should retain task id, environment, observation/action sequence, terminal status, progress checkpoints, progress score, failure type, model/scaffold metadata, and budget. This is valuable for analyzing where an agent stops making progress, not only whether it solved the task.

For atlas curation, use it as a benchmark design example for adding process metrics to environment trajectories. The main reuse boundary is that progress labels and terminal predicates must travel with the task; aggregate scores without their metric definitions are not enough.

AgentBoard 适合作为诊断型轨迹评测 schema。可复用记录应保留 task id、环境、observation/action 序列、终止状态、progress checkpoints、progress score、失败类型、模型/scaffold 元数据和预算。它的用途是分析 agent 在哪里停止推进，而不只是是否解题。

在 atlas 中，可把它作为给环境轨迹加入过程指标的 benchmark 设计样例。主要复用边界是 progress label 和 terminal predicate 必须随任务一起保存；只有聚合分数而没有指标定义是不够的。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
Read the metric definitions together with the environment descriptions. The key distinction is final success versus progress during the episode; they answer different questions and should not be collapsed into one score.

When comparing models, keep base model, agent scaffold, prompts, parsing policy, max turns, and API/tool state separate. A progress advantage can come from better task decomposition alignment, not necessarily from generally better planning.

阅读时要把 metric 定义和环境描述一起看。关键区分是最终成功与 episode 过程中的进展；二者回答不同问题，不能压成一个无解释总分。

比较模型时要分开基础模型、agent scaffold、prompt、解析策略、最大轮数和 API/工具状态。progress 优势可能来自更贴合任务分解，不一定代表通用规划能力更强。
